author: asukhobo
title: GPU unit tests fail to extract OpenVINO package - tbb12.dll locked (Access denied) on Windows self-hosted runner
signature: remove item cannot remove item access to the path is denied unauthorizedaccessexception|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails: Expand-Archive -Force cannot overwrite tbb12.dll because it is locked, PowerShell throws UnauthorizedAccessException.

key_errors: 2026-11-18T06:26:59.6042390Z Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs Expand-Archive -Force against a pre-existing C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install directory left over from a prior job/run on the same self-hosted GPU runner (ov-dmz-58, intel-gpu group). Expand-Archive's -Force cleanup tries to delete the existing tbb12.dll before re-extracting it, but the DLL is still memory-mapped/locked by a lingering process (e.g. an orphaned test or driver process) from a previous job on the same persistent Windows runner, so Remove-Item fails with UnauthorizedAccessException and the step exits with code 1. This is a known, recurring self-hosted-runner hygiene issue (stale workspace + file lock), not a code defect introduced by this PR; the PR's only change (NPU compiler-libs cmake download URL) is unrelated to the GPU extraction step.
reproduction_steps: N/A (requires the specific self-hosted Windows GPU runner state: a stale install/ directory with tbb12.dll locked by a leftover process from a prior job). Not reproducible via a clean local checkout.
recommended_actions: Have the runner/infra team investigate why tbb12.dll remains locked on ov-dmz-58 after prior jobs finish (look for orphaned OpenVINO/test processes or antivirus scanning the install dir).
Add a pre-step to forcibly terminate lingering processes and/or wipe the install/ directory before Expand-Archive runs, instead of relying on -Force to overwrite in place.
Consider extracting to a fresh per-run temp directory rather than reusing a persistent install/ path across runs on the same self-hosted runner.
Re-run the failed GPU unit tests job; this is transient and does not require a code change on PR #39956.
prevention_strategies: Ensure self-hosted Windows GPU runners clean their workspace (kill orphaned processes, remove stale install/test directories) at the start or end of each job rather than depending on Expand-Archive -Force to clobber locked files. Consider running GPU unit test extraction against an isolated/clean directory per run.
historical_context: This exact signature has recurred 12 times (now 13 with this run) since 2026-11-09 across many unrelated PRs (#39900, #39781, #39568, #39653, #39617, #37406, #39577, #39668, #39034, #39444), all on the same class of Windows self-hosted GPU runners during the 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step. A related but distinct signature (stale onednn_third-party-programs.txt blocking Expand-Archive cleanup, pattern e71a74b26eea9146) was seen once on 2026-11-11. Both point to the same underlying self-hosted-runner workspace hygiene problem that has not yet been fixed at the infrastructure level.
